feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report whether the wider ±0.06 m span gives a usable signal with the [-2,-1,0,1,2] weights, or whether the signal gain is now too high (saturation or overshoot). Say whether line losses fell and whether max_error stayed under 0.06 on bends. Say whether slalom steering_oscillation rose above 0.15 and whether the y = 0.03 row still shows lag. Say whether the outer sensors now do useful work or saturate.

intent: Test whether the sensor span is the cause of the early line loss. Widen the outer sensors from ±0.04 m to ±0.06 m (spacing 0.03 m) so the line stays visible out to about 0.07 m of lateral error, past the 0.06 m off-track limit. Keep y = 0.03, the 16 mm footprint, the 0.10 m track, the 0.8 kg mass and the 3 cm wheels fixed, so this race isolates the span change. Expected: line_loss_events fall toward 0, max_error stays below about 0.06, and the robot passes the first bend on the oval and s-bend tracks.
learning: Iteration 1 failed to fix early line loss. Each trial lost the line once and then left the track at about 0.06 m. The line-loss distance matches the outermost sensor's coverage edge (about 0.06 m with ±0.04 m sensors), so the span limits sensing range, not lookahead or footprint. If the wider span cuts line losses but max_error still reaches 0.06 on bends, the next lever is wheel_track 0.12 m (more turn stability) or a higher-gain controller on the Integrator side. If the span change does not reduce line losses, the cause is turn authority, and wheel_track or wheel_radius should be the next geometry change.
rationale: Iteration 1 (y = 0.03, 16 mm sensors, 0.10 m track) changed three things at once and did not change the failure. All 60 trials still went off track after exactly one line-loss event, with max_error about 0.061 to 0.065. The oval and s-bend max_error sat right at the 0.06 m off-track floor, and the slalom steering_oscillation rose to 0.159. Oscillation is now above the Integrator's 0.15 threshold on slalom, but the failure is still early drift, not jitter. The line-loss event is the key clue. With outer sensors at x = ±0.04 and 16 mm footprints, the outermost footprint reaches about 0.048 m from centre. The tape's half-width is 0.0125 m, so the tape stops overlapping any sensor at roughly 0.048 + 0.0125 + ... ≈ 0.06 m of lateral error. That is almost exactly where the robot leaves the track. The sensor span, not the lookahead or footprint, is the most likely limit: the robot loses the line at the same distance it goes off track, so it never gets a reading that would let it recover. The off-track limit cannot be raised by body width (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.18/4) = 0.06 at most), so the fix is to see the line earlier. I will widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.06 with 5 sensors at 0.03 m spacing and keep everything else from iteration 1. This is a single change, so the next race isolates the span effect. The 16 mm footprints with 30 mm spacing leave 14 mm gaps, which the 25 mm tape always spans, so at least one sensor always sees the line. Expected result: line_loss_events fall toward 0 on oval and s-bend, max_error stays below about 0.06, and progress extends past the first bend. Slalom oscillation may stay near or above 0.15 because the wider span raises the signal gain. If it rises above about 0.2, I will move the row to y = 0.02 next.
